selection.ordering: DOI ascending within each domain; first four passing the eligibility checks
eligibility: 150–350 whitespace-delimited words both in the indexed abstract and after publisher XML extraction
English research article; exact publisher XML license URL is Creative Commons Attribution
No author name overlaps across selected articles
No abstract inline-formula, disp-formula, or sup elements
selection.split_assignment: Positions fixed before any generation or detector scoring: ecology 1–2 train/3 dev/4 test; public-health 1–3 train/4 dev; molecular-biology 1–3 train/4 test. Eight train, two dev, two test. Too few sources for domain generalization claims.

extraction.method: Select the first front/article-meta/abstract. For each descendant p in document order, concatenate XML text nodes, collapse Unicode whitespace to one ASCII space, trim, discard empty paragraphs, and join paragraphs with two LF characters. Section/title headings are omitted; inline markup is stripped while its text remains. Do not append a final newline. Raw XML bytes remain available.
extraction.source_kind_rationale: Pre-2020 peer-reviewed publisher articles provide strong historical human-authorship provenance, not absolute proof. Original editorial assistance and model-training contamination are unknown.
human_reference_limitations: One journal, one year, three scientific domains; not representative of general human writing.
Dates concern publication, not exact dates of composition or revision.
Source-conditioned model rewrites share content and may echo originals; their profile does not estimate independent prompt-only generation.
